verses.text: In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in the Italian Regiment.
He was devoted to God, as was his whole household. He gave generously to people in need and prayed to God regularly.
Around three in the afternoon, he clearly saw an angel of God come to him in a vision and call, “Cornelius!”
Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, sir?” The angel said, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have risen as a reminder before God.
“Now send some men to Joppa and bring back Simon, who is also called Peter.
“He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
After the angel left, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier who served him regularly.
He explained everything to them and sent them to Joppa.
The next day, as they were nearing the city, Peter went up to the roof around noon to pray.
He became hungry and wanted something to eat. While the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet coming down to earth, lowered by its four corners.
Inside it were all kinds of four-legged animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
A voice said to him, “Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.”
Peter answered, “Absolutely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything ordinary or unclean.”
The voice spoke to him a second time: “Don’t call anything unclean if God has made it clean.”
This happened three times, and then the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
Peter was puzzled about what his vision meant. Just then the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and stood at the gate.
They called out and asked whether Simon, also known as Peter, was staying there.
While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit told him, “Look, three men are asking for you.
“Get up, go downstairs, and go with them without hesitation. I sent them.”
Peter went down to the men and said, “I’m the one you’re looking for. Why have you come?”

They answered, “Cornelius the centurion sent us. He’s a righteous man who honors God, and the whole Jewish nation respects him. A holy angel told him to invite you to his house and hear what you have to say.”
Peter invited them in and gave them a place to stay. The next day he set out with them, joined by some believers from Joppa.
The following day they arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had gathered his relatives and close friends.
When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and bowed down to him.
But Peter helped him up and said, “Stand up. I’m only a man too.”
As Peter talked with him, he went inside and saw many people gathered there.
He said to them, “You know it’s against our law for a Jew to associate with someone from another nation or visit them. But God has shown me I must not call any person polluted or unclean.
“So when you sent for me, I came without objecting. Now tell me why you asked me to come.”
Cornelius replied, “Four days ago, at this same hour, I was praying in my house at three in the afternoon. Suddenly a man in bright clothing stood in front of me
“and said, ‘Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and remembered your gifts to the poor.
“‘Send someone to Joppa and invite Simon, also called Peter. He is staying in the home of Simon the tanner by the sea. When he arrives, he will speak to you.’
“So I sent for you right away, and it was good of you to come. Now we’re all here before God, ready to hear everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.”
Peter began to speak: “Now I truly understand that God doesn’t play favorites.
“In every nation, anyone who honors him and does what is right is welcome to him.
“God sent his message to Israel, announcing the Good News of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
“You know what happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee after John preached baptism:
“God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. He went around doing good and healing everyone oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
“We are witnesses of everything he did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree,
“but God raised him on the third day and allowed him to be seen.
“He wasn’t shown to everyone, but to witnesses God had chosen beforehand—to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
“He commanded us to preach to the people and testify that God appointed him as judge of the living and the dead.
“All the prophets testify about him: everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”
While Peter was still saying this, the Holy Spirit came upon everyone who heard the message.
The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the Holy Spirit’s gift had also been poured out on Gentiles.
They heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Then Peter said,
“Can anyone keep these people from being baptized in water? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.”
So he ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay with them for several days.
